newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Allegiance sees EPS gains.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Allegiance sees EPS gains.

text.p: Allegiance Corp, spun off from Baxter International Inc, expects earnings growth in the high single digits as it focuses on its higher-margin businesses, executives said on Tuesday.
"We think earnings will grow in the high single digits for the foreseeable future," Allegiance Chief Executive Lester Knight said in an interview.
He said the health-care products and cost-management company was "pretty comfortable" with analysts' estimates for its 1996 earnings per share in a range of $1.00 to $1.05.
He also backed analysts' forecasts of 1997 EPS in the $1.15-to-$1.20 range.
The mean Wall Street estimates are for the company to earn $1.03 a share in 1996 and $1.17 a share in 1997, according to First Call.
Shares in Allegiance Corp began trading on Tuesday following a spinoff announced last year.
The stock was off 1/4 at 17-3/4 by 1240 EDT/1640 GMT Tuesday.

"In the short term we are going through a transition where we're trying to push the higher-margin products and programs," Knight said. Those include its medical products manufacturing and hospital cost-management businesses.
The company is looking to "really slow down the growth, if not even shed some of the lower margin contracts we have out in the marketplace and get our margins stabilized," he said.
A fight for market share among Allegiance, Owens & Minor and General Medical has driven down prices in the health-care products distribution business.
During the past eight or nine months Allegiance has stepped back from that fight and has begun to raise prices in the products distribution business, Knight said.
He said the company did not "need" to expand its 30 to 40 percent market share in the laboratory and surgical supply markets but needed to improve its profitability and return.
Knight declined to give profit margin figures but said the products distribution business had a return on assets of four to six percent.
Its health-care products manufacturing business, meanwhile, is showing a return of 15 to 20 percent, while hospital cost-management services has a return of more than 20 percent.

Of the company's annual sales of about $4.5 billion, about $3.0 billion comes from the distribution business, while the manufacturing unit accounts for most of the remainder. The cost-management unit is currently a "small piece" that Allegiance hopes to expand, Knight said.
Allegiance executives said they expected the company to generate a total of $500 million in free cash flow during the next five years.
It will use the money for investments including acquisitions and new product research and development as well as to pay down debt, they said.
The company's debt stands at $1.2 billion and its debt-to-capital ratio is 46 percent. Its aim is to drive the ratio down to between 40 and 45 percent, the executives said.
